subtitle: When Hoysala poets bent sound and story, Kannada found new wings

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a Hoysala temple courtyard filled with palm-leaf manuscripts and reciting poets, stone lions looming overhead
panels.action: Janna stands in a sunlit Halebidu courtyard, manuscripts in hand, as unseen voices of Harihara and Raghavanka echo around carved pillars and lion friezes of a great Hoysala temple.

dialogue.text: In the age of the Hoysalas, Janna, Harihara and Raghavanka dared to bend metre and morals—so Kannada could stand beside Sanskrit, and speak to both court and commoner.

i18n.hi: होयसालों के दौर में जन्ना, हरिहरा और राघवंक ने छंद और नीति दोनों को तोड़ा—ताकि कन्नड़ संस्कृत के साथ खड़ी हो सके, राजदरबार और आम जन दोनों से बोल सके।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over Halebidu, transitioning from gleaming temple towers to the royal court hall
panels.action: A high view of Halebidu shows star-shaped Hoysala temples and the royal audience hall where scholars gather, palm leaves stacked beside a Sanskrit court poet and a Kannada scribe.

dialogue.text: Under the Hoysala kings, Sanskrit praised, Kannada recorded. Inscriptions split their duties: lofty prashasti in Sanskrit, practical grants in Kannada, written on stone in the same courtyard.

i18n.hi: होयसाल राजाओं के समय, संस्कृत ने जयगान किया, कन्नड़ ने हाल दर्ज किए। शिलालेखों ने काम बाँट लिया: ऊँची प्रशस्ति संस्कृत में, ज़मीनी दान-पत्र कन्नड़ में—एक ही आँगन की पत्थर पर।

panels.shot: slow push-in inside the court hall onto a stone inscription being carved by an artisan as a scholar dictates
panels.action: A sculptor chisels a stone slab as a court scholar recites Sanskrit eulogy first and then switches to Kannada clauses for land grants, the rhythm of hammer and voice filling the hall.

dialogue.text: Sheldon Pollock would later call this shift vernacularization: the long, careful turning of Kannada into a language of rule, ritual and poetry alongside the old tongue of the gods.

i18n.hi: शेल्डन पोलॉक ने बाद में इसे ‘देशभाषीकरण’ कहा: कन्नड़ को धीरे-धीरे राज, धर्म और कविता की भाषा बनाना, देवताओं की पुरानी ज़बान के साथ-साथ।

panels.shot: medium shot in a quieter corner of the court where Janna sits cross-legged with Jain monks and patrons
panels.action: Janna sits cross-legged on a woven mat, Jain monks beside him, a Hoysala patron listening, while he gently traces Kannada verses onto a fresh palm leaf.

dialogue.text: Within this world, poets like Janna, Harihara and Raghavanka listened to stone and scripture—and asked, how can Kannada carry subtle ethics, fierce devotion, and new music of its own?

i18n.hi: इसी दुनिया में जन्ना, हरिहरा और राघवंक जैसे कवि पत्थर और शास्त्र से सुनते रहे—और पूछते रहे, कन्नड़ कैसे सूक्ष्म नैतिकता, तीखी भक्ति और अपनी नई लय को सँभाले?

panels.shot: close-up of Janna’s hand writing on palm leaf, with a faint overlay of temple sculpture in the background
panels.action: Janna’s steady hand inscribes rounded Kannada letters on a palm leaf, the faint outline of a Jina statue and Hoysala carvings behind him suggesting Jain and courtly worlds intertwined.

dialogue.text: Around 1209 CE, Janna completed Yashodhara Charite, a Jain narrative in Kannada. It married courtly polish with stark ethical dilemmas, pressing language to bear the weight of conscience.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1209 ई. में जन्ना ने ‘यशोधर चरिते’ पूरी की, कन्नड़ में जैन कथा। दरबारी निखार और कड़वे नैतिक द्वंद्व साथ आए, भाषा को अंतरात्मा का बोझ उठाने पर मजबूर किया।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot of Janna reciting in a hall, patrons and monks listening tensely
panels.action: Janna stands to recite before a small gathering; his raised hand marks a beat as listeners lean in, their faces tense at a moral turning point in the story.

dialogue.text: His tale of Yashodhara and his wife turns on cruel choices, karmic consequence and compassion. The metre must carry not just sound, but shock, pity, and the quiet questions that follow.

i18n.hi: यशोधर और उसकी पत्नी की कथा क्रूर चुनावों, कर्मफल और करुणा पर घूमती है। छंद को सिर्फ ध्वनि नहीं, झटका, दया और बाद की खामोश सवाल भी ढोने थे।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Janna’s thoughtful face, half-lit by a lamp, suggesting inner struggle
panels.action: In lamplight, Janna pauses mid-composition, eyes closed, as if weighing each syllable against the ethical weight of the scene he shapes.

dialogue.speaker: Janna
dialogue.text: If the metre is rigid, how will this pain reach their hearts?

i18n.hi: अगर छंद जकड़ा रहे, तो ये पीड़ा उनके दिल तक कैसे पहुँचेगी?

panels.shot: transition shot from Janna’s palm leaf to another poet’s palm leaf, hinting at Harihara, with rhythmic marks
panels.action: The frame shifts from Janna’s script to another palm leaf where lines are spaced irregularly, marked with rhythmic dots, suggesting the looser flow of ragale verse.

dialogue.text: Even before Janna’s work, Harihara’s ragale poems had begun to loosen older metrical bonds, giving Kannada lines a more rolling, chant-like rhythm closer to spoken feeling.

i18n.hi: जन्ना से पहले ही हरिहरा की रगले कविताएँ पुराने छंद की कसावट ढीली कर रही थीं, कन्नड़ पंक्तियों को बोलचाल के एहसास के करीब बहती, जप जैसी लय दे रही थीं।

panels.shot: imagined medium shot of Harihara reciting ragale outdoors near a shrine, villagers around him
panels.action: A bearded poet figure stands before a small shrine, beating time with his palm against his thigh as villagers sway to a ragale chant in Kannada, the lines flowing without strict end-rhymes.

dialogue.text: In Basavarajadevara Ragale, Harihara sang of Basava’s life in flowing ragale. Devotional biography met flexible metre, bringing reform and bhakti into the cadences of everyday speech.

i18n.hi: ‘बसवराजदेवर रगले’ में हरिहरा ने बसव की कथा बहते रगले में गाई। भक्तिमय जीवनचरित लचीले छंद से मिला, सुधार और भक्ति को रोज़ की बोलचाल की ताल में उतार दिया।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of a temple corridor where echoes of ragale verse meet the silence of carved walls
panels.action: A long temple corridor, its stone walls carved with dancers and deities, hums with faint imagined echoes of ragale recitation, as if new metre is testing itself against ancient stone.

dialogue.text: Ragale softened hard edges of older forms. Lines could stretch, rush, slow. With this, Kannada grew better at telling movement and mood, not only static praise or rigid doctrine.

i18n.hi: रगले ने पुराने रूपों की कड़ी धार नरम की। पंक्तियाँ फैल सकती थीं, दौड़ सकती थीं, थम सकती थीं। इससे कन्नड़ हरकत और मन:स्थिति सुनाने में माहिर हुई, सिर्फ जड़ स्तुति या सख़्त मत नहीं।

panels.shot: smooth pan to another recitation space where a poet voices six-beat lines, hinting at shatpadi
panels.action: In a different hall, a poet figure counts on his fingers as he recites lines with a clear six-part rhythm, listeners nodding to the pattern like a remembered song.

dialogue.text: Soon, Raghavanka’s Harishchandra Kavya would make the six-line shatpadi famous. Each stanza a measured wave, perfect for long narrative, lament, and moral drama.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही राघवंक का ‘हरिश्चंद्र काव्य’ छह पंक्तियों वाले शट्पदी को मशहूर कर देगा। हर स्तवक जैसे नापी हुई लहर—लंबी कथा, विलाप और नैतिक नाटक के लिए बिल्कुल ठीक।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of an imagined scene from Harishchandra’s story being enacted before an audience
panels.action: Actors on a simple stage enact King Harishchandra’s suffering as a poet chants shatpadi verses nearby; the audience sits spellbound, some wiping tears, swept by the rhythm and story.

dialogue.text: Harishchandra’s truth against unbearable loss needed a strong yet flexible frame. Shatpadi carried this, each six-lined pulse stepping the listener deeper into the king’s ordeal.

i18n.hi: हरिश्चंद्र की सच की लड़ाई, असहनीय क्षति के बीच, मज़बूत पर लचीले ढाँचे माँगती थी। शट्पदी ने यह सँभाला, हर छह-पंक्तियों की धड़कन सुनने वाले को राजा की पीड़ा में और भीतर ले गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of court scholars debating between Sanskrit and Kannada manuscripts on a low table
panels.action: Around a low table, scholars compare a Sanskrit manuscript with Kannada palm leaves of ragale and shatpadi; fingers point, heads nod, the debate lively but respectful.

dialogue.text: Sanskrit did not vanish from Hoysala halls. It framed royal glory and rite. Yet Kannada, with Janna, Harihara and Raghavanka, now claimed space for ethics, emotion and experiment.

i18n.hi: संस्कृत होयसाल दरबार से ग़ायब नहीं हुई। वही राज-वैभव और कर्मकांड की चौखट रही। पर जन्ना, हरिहरा और राघवंक के साथ कन्नड़ ने अब नीति, भावना और प्रयोग की अपनी जगह बना ली।

panels.shot: close-up on a stone inscription combining Sanskrit and Kannada in different sections
panels.action: A single inscription slab shows decorative, compact Sanskrit at the top and clearer, practical Kannada below, the change in script style visible along one smooth stone surface.

dialogue.text: On stone, Sanskrit prashasti and Kannada clauses shared space. In verse, new Kannada metres shared air with older forms. Power and poetry began to recognize two trusted voices.

i18n.hi: पत्थर पर संस्कृत प्रशस्ति और कन्नड़ धाराएँ साथ-साथ उकेरी गईं। छंद में नए कन्नड़ रूप पुराने से कंधा मिला कर चले। सत्ता और कविता ने दो भरोसेमंद आवाज़ों को पहचानना शुरू किया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Janna, seated among younger scribes, guiding their recitation rhythm
panels.action: Janna sits with younger scribes and poets, tapping a gentle beat on the floor as they recite lines, correcting their cadence with a calm, precise gesture.

dialogue.speaker: Janna
dialogue.text: Let the story choose its metre. Then shape the metre with care.

i18n.hi: कहानी को अपना छंद चुनने दो—फिर छंद को प्यार से तराशो।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot of different Kannada manuscripts—Jain narrative, ragale, shatpadi—arrayed on a mat
panels.action: On a woven mat, palm leaves of Yashodhara Charite, ragale hymns, and shatpadi narrative lie side by side, their scripts similar but their spacing and line breaks clearly different.

dialogue.text: Jain ethical tales, Shaiva devotion, royal biography—all pressed Kannada to stretch. New metres were not mere ornament. They were tools for new kinds of thought and feeling.

i18n.hi: जैन नैतिक कथाएँ, शैव भक्ति, राज-जीवनचरित—सबने कन्नड़ को खिंच कर फैलाया। नए छंद सिर्फ सजावट नहीं थे; वे सोच और भावना के नए औज़ार बने।

panels.shot: high-angle shot of Halebidu at dusk, temple silhouettes and distant voices of chanting
panels.action: At dusk, Halebidu’s carved towers stand in silhouette as distant, overlapping Kannada chants rise from temple, home and court, forming a textured sonic tapestry over the city.

dialogue.text: By the early thirteenth century, the Hoysala realm heard Kannada not just in village talk, but in polished courtly verse and public recitation. A new literary soundscape had taken hold.

i18n.hi: तेरहवीं सदी की शुरुआत तक होयसाल राज्य में कन्नड़ सिर्फ गाँव की बोली नहीं, सँवरी दरबारी कविता और सार्वजनिक पाठ की भाषा भी बन चुकी थी। एक नया साहित्यिक साउंडस्केप जम गया था।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on a modern reader’s hand touching an old Kannada manuscript in a museum
panels.action: A modern hand reaches out under soft museum light to hover just above a preserved palm-leaf manuscript of Old Kannada verse, the faded letters still clear and graceful.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, those metres still carry. Ragale and shatpadi shape schoolbooks and stage plays; Janna’s ethical tremors echo in fresh retellings of old Jain and royal stories.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद भी वे छंद चलते रहे। रगले और शट्पदी आज स्कूल की किताबों और मंच नाटकों की काया गढ़ते हैं; जन्ना की नैतिक कंपकंपी नई जैन और राजकथाओं की ताज़ा रीटेलिंग में गूँजती है।

panels.shot: wide contemplative shot of a contemporary Kannada poet writing by window, faint ghostly figures of Janna, Harihara, Raghavanka behind
panels.action: A present-day Kannada poet writes at a window overlooking Karnataka’s hills, while faint, respectful silhouettes of Janna, Harihara and Raghavanka stand behind like guardians of metre.

dialogue.text: A language grows when poets dare to reshape it: the Hoysalas’ Kannada masters show that every new rhythm we risk today might become tomorrow’s enduring voice of justice, devotion and joy.

i18n.hi: भाषा तब बढ़ती है जब कवि उसे नया रूप देने की हिम्मत रखते हैं: होयसालों के कन्नड़ उस्ताद दिखाते हैं कि आज जो नई लय हम आज़माएँ, वही कल न्याय, भक्ति और आनंद की टिकाऊ आवाज़ बन सकती है।

title_i18n.hi: कन्नड़ सीखती नई छंद की चाल

subtitle_i18n.en: When Hoysala poets bent sound and story, Kannada found new wings
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब होयसाल कवियों ने ध्वनि और कथा मोड़ी, कन्नड़ को मिल गए नए पंख
